result.title: Toward a digital twin of the ICU patient: Forecasting and treatment response in a generative event model
result.summary: A digital twin of a patient in intensive care would forecast the patient's course and what a treatment would change. Generative event models, trained to continue a patient's electronic health record (EHR), have been proposed as a path toward such twins. We trained TWICE, a 79M-parameter decoder-only transformer, on the ICU records of one academic health system (127,332 training patients and 1.57 billion tokens). We evaluated it on clinical prediction tasks, generation fidelity, individual trajectories and counterfactual validation. Reading 19 clinical outcomes off 50 simulated futures, with no task-specific training, TWICE matched the best of 144 supervised configurations on held-out patients (mean AUROC 0.836 vs. 0.834). It led on events that change care within a day and trailed on death. With the training data fixed, more and longer simulated futures were worth more than a 6.8-fold larger model. Its generated records matched real ones closely and were as specific to each patient as its own variability allowed. Its predicted risk rose as events approached. Pre-specified controls showed that it reproduced the side effects of drugs and was barely moved by an inert drug. On the values that treatments are given to correct, however, an opposite treatment moved its forecasts like the right one. TWICE forecasts ICU events about as well as task-specific models, and we see it as a step toward a digital twin of the ICU patient.

AI.brief_summary: 训练 79M 参数的 decoder-only transformer TWICE，在单家医疗系统约 12.7 万 ICU 病人的电子病历上做生成式事件续写；仅靠从 50 条模拟未来中读出 19 项临床结局（无任务微调）即接近最强监督基线，并评估生成保真度与反事实治疗响应。
AI.relevance_reason: 「多采样模拟未来聚合出答案、增加采样比放大模型更划算」可供核查 LVR 中动态采样与潜状态推演的算力分配；其反事实对照中反向治疗也被判为有效，则提示 latent 因果贡献评估的失败风险。
